questions.stem: Highfield Bakery, a regional firm estimates that a Westhaven customer generates $29 in annual contribution margin and that the annual retention rate is 80 percent. Using a simple perpetuity approximation, what is the customer lifetime value?
questions.explanation: In a simple retention-based lifetime value model, CLV equals annual contribution margin divided by the churn rate, where churn is one minus the retention rate. With churn of 20 percent, that is $29 divided by 0.20, giving about $145. Multiplying by a fixed number of years ignores that customers can leave at any time, and multiplying by churn is the wrong direction.
questions.hint: Divide annual margin by one minus the retention rate.
questions.learningObjective: compute a simple customer lifetime value

options.misconception: multiplies by churn instead of dividing by it
divides by the number of years, which the simple model does not use
ignores retention and just multiplies by a fixed life

questions.subject: MARKETING
questions.stem: Customers of Redstone Bags, a family-owned firm in Harborview praise the staff's courtesy and willingness to help. Which service-quality dimension does this reflect?
questions.explanation: Service quality is commonly described by dimensions including reliability, responsiveness, empathy, assurance and tangibles. Courtesy and willingness to help are about responsiveness and empathy, the human side of service. Tangibles concern the physical environment, and reliability concerns delivering the promised service dependably.
questions.hint: Courtesy and helping behaviour are about how staff treat customers.

options.text: Tangibles such as facilities and equipment
options.misconception: confuses people-related cues with physical evidence
mistakes an interpersonal dimension for a price judgement
assumes the praise concerns consistent delivery

options.text: Responsiveness and empathy of the service staff
